issues: The world was the generic grey FakeDashboard: five rows of grey placeholder bars and squares, with no readable text in the close-up, so the viewer never learns what "this row" is
The 3.2x opening close-up showed two huge blank cards, like a zoomed wireframe; frame one was not a designed image
The pulled-back final frame was a full page of grey bars with no title, number or hero, so "this row is one cell of a whole wall" never reads
Row pulses were faint grey washes, almost invisible on the grey-white page; after reaching full frame the shot froze for 30f, a dead hold
changes: Porcelain look (cool white, cobalt, teal accent): the world is rebuilt as a shot-designed logistics app window, "Relay", with top bar, Shipments header, a 104px in-transit KPI and 12 realistic shipment rows (ID, route, carrier, ETA, status pill, progress, weight)

In the 3.0x close-up the ID and route are 63px type; a focus pull keeps only the tracked row sharp (cobalt tint, breathing tracking dot) with other rows at 38%, restoring over 26f once the crane lifts

The crane move is kept (one bezier(0.2,0,0.25,1) drives scale 3.0 to 1 and the focus point); a cobalt sweep crosses each row from its start as the top of frame passes it, and the fast segment gets CameraMotionBlur

Sense of scale: the KPI counts 0 to 48,210 in sync with the pull; the window shadow lifts to a floating height and a background dot grid moves at 0.35 parallax, so the end frame reads as a product sitting on a porcelain stage
The hold gets one small event: the tracked row springs to a teal "Delivered" pill with a drawn check and a filled progress bar; duration 150 to 165f
